Title.Emphasis: Sums adjudged to be paid by a conviction

P1group.Title: Restrictions on power to order immediate committal in default of payment of a sum adjudged to be paid by a conviction

P2para.Text: A warrant committing a person to prison in respect of non-payment of a sum adjudged to be paid by a conviction of a magistrates' court shall not be issued at the time of his conviction unless—

P3para.Text: he appears to the court to have sufficient means to pay the sum forthwith; or
on being asked by the court whether he wishes to have time for payment he does not ask for time; or
the court is satisfied that he has no fixed abode in Northern Ireland; or
there is some other special circumstance appearing to the court to justify immediate committal;

P1para.Text: and if the court does issue a warrant of commitment, the court shall state in the warrant the reasons for not allowing the person committed time to pay.

Text.Addition: This Article does not apply where the person is a child.

Para.Text: Pt. IX (arts. 91-117) applied (1.10.2009) by Criminal Justice and Immigration Act 2008 (c. 4), ss. 88(6)(7), 153(4)(d); S.I. 2009/2606, art. 2(i)
